done.why: I went through the curtain of light carrying the portrait and landed in a Small Room with no exits. Waiting, yelling, dropping things and talking to the gnome didn't get me out.

about: A Zork II style cave. The Wizard of Frobozz has scattered the Empire's treasures south of the ravine, and he tricks you with illusions and curses. I met a fake grue, a fake gold ingot, a dragon, a carousel room, and the Bank of Zork with its vault puzzle.

ending.what: None. I took the Chairman's portrait but never got it out of the bank.

moments.note: The grue was an illusion cast by the Wizard, and the sword went through it.
I couldn't take the gold ingot. It seems to have been an illusion too.
The bank's doorways bar you when you carry the portrait, but the curtain of light doesn't.
Small Room with no exits. I couldn't find any way out.
The carousel room's exits were inconsistent and mostly led back to the Marble Hall.

wished: A clue about how to get out of the Small Room.
A clearer sense of what to do with the treasure once I had it.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you.
the Bank built its doorways to know its own property going through them

fun.why: The early exploring and the bank puzzle were good. Getting trapped in the Small Room was a dead end.

engagement.why: The Wizard's tricks and the bank held my interest until I got stuck.

difficulty.why: The Small Room gave me no way out and no hints.

interestingness.why: The Wizard's illusions and the bank doorway logic were clever.

prose.why: Witty, with wry explanations of the illusions.
